idiom_name: type with non-public constructor(s) + class-level creation operations named after the construction intent
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: keep the constructors out of the public API and expose one creation operation per distinct construction intent, named after that intent rather than after its parameters. The operation validates its inputs, may return a cached or preconstructed instance, may choose a concrete subtype or keep an implementation class hidden, and returns the least specific type that carries the contract; it must state whether repeated calls may return the same instance. Where construction can fail, the operation returns an error or optional value instead of a half-built object. Decide up front whether subclassing stays possible (keep a protected constructor) or whether the non-public constructor deliberately closes the type.
code_sketch:
type T with non-public constructor      # invariant: only the named routes create T
T.create_a(...)      -> T              # validates, may hit the cache
T.create_from_b(...) -> Result<T, E>   # failure as a value, no half-built object
T.create_for_c(...)  -> Base           # may return a hidden implementation subtype
# callers never construct T directly; identity semantics are documented per route
pitfalls: Leaving a public constructor next to the factories creates a bypass route, and any invariant the factories enforce stops being an invariant of the type.
Caching instances without documenting identity semantics lets callers rely on object identity where the type never promised it (or mutate a shared instance by accident).
Turning creation into a static utility that performs hidden I/O, registration or global lookup couples every call site to configuration the factory quietly reads.

Wrong move: expose `new T(...)` beside named factories -> callers can bypass validation and create states the routes forbid -> instead make the raw constructor non-public or reserve it for trusted subclasses.

Wrong move: return cached mutable instances without documenting identity -> one caller's mutation leaks to others and identity checks become accidental API contracts -> instead return immutable values, document sharing, and bound or synchronize the cache.

Wrong move: let a `from` or `create` route read global configuration or perform I/O silently -> call sites acquire hidden dependencies and tests become order- or configuration-dependent -> instead use a context-owned factory or an explicit `open`/`load` operation that exposes failure.
